original_question: Let X1 and X2 be prime Fano threefolds of index 1 and degree 10, so in particular Gushel-Mukai threefolds. If there is a Fourier-Mukai type equivalence Phi: Ku(X1) -> Ku(X2), must X1 and X2 be birational?
target_in_paper: Section 6.5, Question 6.34 ([67], Question 1.1(1)): the birational categorical Torelli question for degree-10 prime Fano threefolds, i.e. Gushel-Mukai threefolds.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's official formulation almost verbatim. It has the correct class of varieties (prime Fano threefolds of index 1 and degree 10, hence Gushel-Mukai threefolds), the correct categorical hypothesis (an equivalence Ku(X1) ≅ Ku(X2) of Fourier-Mukai type), and the correct conclusion (birationality). It also stays at the exact scope of the paper's open problem rather than drifting to a broader neighboring conjecture.
missing_details: The paper states Section 6.5 under the simplifying assumption that the base field is C, so the ambient field should be made explicit for a fully paper-faithful stand-alone version.

Ku(X_i) should be defined explicitly as the Kuznetsov component appearing in the standard semiorthogonal decomposition D^b(X_i)=<Ku(X_i), E_{2,i}, O_{X_i}> for degree-10 index-1 prime Fano threefolds.
For full self-containment, 'prime Fano threefold of index 1 and degree 10' should be unpacked as a smooth projective Fano threefold X with Pic(X)=Z·H, -K_X=H, and H^3=10.
The hypothesis should specify that Phi is an exact equivalence of triangulated categories.

The phrase 'of Fourier-Mukai type' should be tied to Definition 2.6: namely, the functor is induced by a kernel on X1 x X2 after composing with the admissible embeddings of the Kuznetsov components into the bounded derived categories.
refined_question: Working over C, let X1 and X2 be smooth prime Fano threefolds of Picard rank 1, index 1, and degree 10; equivalently, if Pic(X_i)=Z·H_i, then -K_{X_i}=H_i and H_i^3=10, so X_i is a Gushel-Mukai threefold. Let Ku(X_i) be the Kuznetsov component in the standard semiorthogonal decomposition D^b(X_i)=<Ku(X_i), E_{2,i}, O_{X_i}>. If there exists an exact equivalence Phi: Ku(X1) -> Ku(X2) of Fourier-Mukai type in the sense of Definition 2.6, must X1 and X2 be birational?
justification: The nearest official formulation of your draft is exactly Section 6.5, Question 6.34. The surrounding discussion identifies the degree-10 case with Gushel-Mukai threefolds, fixes the paper's local base field convention for this section to C, and places the question immediately after a stronger refined Torelli statement that requires preservation of the distinguished object i^!(E_r) in order to deduce isomorphism. Because your draft asks only for birationality from an equivalence of Kuznetsov components, the right refinement is to make the field, the definition of Ku(X), and the meaning of 'Fourier-Mukai type' explicit, without adding that extra preservation hypothesis and without broadening to the later all-dimensional Gushel-Mukai conjecture.
